_README: PROVISIONAL DECISION REGISTER — the single source of truth for decisions that were taken on a SMALL trade sample and must be revisited once more closed trades exist. This file is read by research/decision_review.py and the .github/workflows/decision_review.yml scheduled job, which opens a persistent GitHub issue (and pings Telegram) the moment a decision becomes due. Do NOT track schedules in prose anywhere else — add an entry here instead, so the human-read path and the automated path can never drift. See AGENTS.md > 'Provisional Decision Register' for the mandatory process. Entries are of two KINDS. A 'parameter' entry is a tuned number awaiting more evidence; a 'work-item' entry is a piece of engineering work deliberately deferred until the bot is in a safe state to absorb it. Both use `revisit` as the trigger (when to look), and may additionally declare `preconditions` (whether it is safe to act today) which are evaluated against LIVE portfolio state. A due-but-blocked entry is still reported -- never silently skipped.

_schema.id: kebab-case unique key; also the GitHub-issue marker
_schema.title: one-line human label
_schema.status: active | resolved | superseded  (only 'active' is ever alerted on)
_schema.implemented: bool — true once the decision is live in production code; false = approved config still on the shelf
_schema.decision: what we decided to do, stated as current fact
_schema.rationale: why, and on how large a sample
_schema.adr: path to the ADR that records the reasoning (may be null until written)

revisit.min_closed_trades: int | null — becomes due once trade_history has >= this many rows
revisit.not_before: YYYY-MM-DD | null — a date floor; due only once BOTH this and min_closed_trades are satisfied

_schema.baseline: the numbers measured at decision time, so a future review compares like-for-like
_schema.review_command: the exact command that reproduces the measurement
_schema.review_questions: the specific questions the review must answer
_schema.last_reviewed: YYYY-MM-DD | null — set when a review is completed
_schema.history: append-only log of {date, closed_trades, verdict, note} from each completed review
_schema.kind: parameter | work-item | investigation  -- 'parameter' is a tuned value awaiting more trades; 'work-item' is deferred engineering work; 'investigation' is an OPEN QUESTION to be settled by measurement, where 'no signal, do nothing' is a valid and expected outcome. Defaults to 'parameter' when absent, so pre-existing entries are unaffected.

preconditions._note: OPTIONAL. Evaluated against live portfolio state at review time. This is the 'is it safe to act TODAY' check, separate from `revisit` which is the 'is it time' trigger. Omit the block entirely for no constraint.
preconditions.max_open_positions: int | null -- actionable only when open positions <= this. Use 0 to require a flat book.
preconditions.min_position_age_days: int | null -- actionable only when the YOUNGEST open position is at least this many days old. A flat book always satisfies this. Youngest is the binding one: a single day-0 position sits in the tight Prove-It Phase 1 band, so the book is not quiet.

decisions.title: Partial scale-out: sell 33% at +4% peak gain
decisions.decision: When an open position's PEAK gain first reaches +4%, sell 33% of the shares at market; the remaining ~67% rides the unchanged Prove-It stop. Fires once per position (scaled_out latch); suppressed for power-held leaders. Freed capital stays as reserve until a full slot opens, then redeploys via normal available_cash / remaining_slots sizing. Live in execute_scale_out() + monitor_portfolio_intraday(); ADR and docs shipped.
decisions.rationale: Chosen on a 33-closed-trade exit replay. +4%/33% was net-free vs the shipped Prove-It stop (-$64, deep in noise), had the lowest harmed count (6), and captured the winner->loser give-back band with the benefit SPREAD over 3 trades (LPG +$317, SGHC +$514, CDNA +$275) rather than carried by one. 33% over 50% because the replay understates runner upside (bars stop at each trade's actual sell), so over-booking has a hidden cost. KNOWN LIMITATION: it rescues only 3 of 7 faders; GNK (+2.85%) and FRO (+3.91%) peaked below +4% and are NOT helped — those are an entry-quality problem, tracked separately.
review_questions: Does +4%/33% still match or beat the SHIPPED net? (was -$64 = free)
Is the fader benefit still spread over >=3 trades, or is it now carried by one? (single-trade-carry check)
Has the winner-clip grown — is harmed or winners_hurt higher than the baseline 6?
Do enough faders now peak in the +4-5% band to justify the trigger, or has the fader distribution shifted (argue the trigger up/down with the new peaks)?
Would a different fraction (25% / 50%) now win, given the larger sample?

decisions.title: Cooling-off re-entry block held at 3 days (not 7, not retired)
decisions.decision: COOLING_OFF_DAYS defaults to 3 in config.py and .env.template, matching what production has run via a .env override since before 2026-08-09. Buy gate 2 continues to block re-entry for 3 days after a sale, checking BOTH trade_history and ibkr_fills SLD fills. The gate is NOT retired.
decisions.rationale: Measured on 9 genuine re-entries (43 closed trades) plus a 26-trigger FMP counterfactual. 7 days blocks 7 of the 9 re-entries, worth +$1,736.67 net (4 winners / 3 losers, winners ~5x losers), including NTRA's 4-day re-entry of 2026-09-14 (+$575.44) — so 7 is measurably too wide, and its original justification in the 2026-08-09 ADR was asserted, never measured. But 0 is worse: of 26 blocked re-entries with forward bars, 16 (62%) break the Prove-It 1% day-0 band on their FIRST session, so the headline +2.17% mean 5-day return is unreachable — the bot exits on the band long before it. 0 also re-enables the same-session churn (NTRA sold 10:26, re-bought 10:32) that corrupted the lot basis. MAJOR CONFOUND: SLOTS_FULL accounts for 115 of 214 logged skips vs COOLING_OFF's 28, so capacity is the real binding constraint and +$1,736.67 is an UPPER BOUND on what 7 costs, not realised foregone profit. Sample is one month, entirely inside a BULL regime.
decisions.review_command: set -a && . ~/.config/ai-trading-bot/secrets.env && set +a && python3 research/exit_rule_replay.py --insecure && python3 research/decision_review.py --insecure
review_questions: How many GENUINE re-entries now exist? (was 9; exclude split-fill duplicates sharing a buy timestamp, e.g. the TRV 2026-07-21 pair.) Below ~25 the comparison is still noise — report n FIRST.
Would a 7-day rule still be net-negative? (was -$1,736.67 across 7 blocked re-entries.) Is that result still spread across several trades, or is it now carried by one outlier like LPG's +$882?
Does the 62% day-0-band break rate still hold for triggers the 3-day gate blocks? If it has fallen well below ~40%, retirement becomes arguable and should be swept properly.
Sweep 2, 3, 4 and 5 days — not just 3 vs 7 vs 0. Adjacent values were never discriminated because the sample was too small.
Has the bot traded through a non-BULL regime yet? The entire decision sample sits inside one bull window; a corrective tape is the real test of whether fast re-entry is safe.
Has the SLOTS_FULL confound shrunk? If capacity is still the binding constraint (was 115 of 214 skips), the dollar figures remain an upper bound and should be quoted as such.

decisions.title: Shadow rs_percentile: measure relative-strength ranking without trading on it
decisions.decision: The screener computes and stores three research-only columns on daily_triggers and trigger_history: rs_12w_return, rs_excess_return (unclipped excess vs SPY) and rs_percentile (1-99 rank within that run's trigger cohort). compute_rs_score() and compute_final_score() are UNCHANGED and no buy gate, sort order, position size or exit rule reads any of the three. This is pure instrumentation: the bot trades exactly as it did before. tests/test_rs_percentile.py asserts compute_final_score's signature contains none of the shadow columns, so the day someone wires the percentile into live scoring, this register entry is invalidated by a failing test.
decisions.rationale: compute_rs_score() clips to a flat 100 for any excess >= +10% vs SPY. The watchlist is already pre-filtered to growth names near 52-week highs, so 176 of 233 archived triggers (76%) score exactly 100 - the component cannot rank three of every four candidates, and its 10% weight in final_score does almost no discriminating work. That defect is established. The SIGN of the repair is NOT: within a universe already filtered for momentum, every sample we hold points the other way. corr(rs_score, fwd_20d) = -0.68 on the 16 labelled rows; losers entered with HIGHER mean 12-week returns than winners (31.1% vs 28.1%) over 48 closed trades; and the single largest loss in the book (CDNA, -$1,539) entered the most extended at +121%. A 'correct' percentile that promotes the strongest name could therefore buy more CDNAs. Crucially the -0.68 rests on 16 rows that all share ONE trigger date (2026-08-14) - effectively one observation, not sixteen. Shipping shadow mode buys a real multi-date sample without touching live selection during a profitable run (post-Prove-It: n=17, +$3,527, 59% win, worst loss -$280).
decisions.review_command: set -a && . ~/.config/ai-trading-bot/secrets.env && set +a && python3 backfill_trigger_outcomes.py && python3 research/rs_percentile_review.py --insecure
review_questions: How many trigger_history rows now carry BOTH rs_percentile and a non-null fwd_20d_pct, and across how many DISTINCT trigger dates? Below ~5 distinct dates this is still one cohort wearing a disguise - report the date count first, every time, and skip rather than read noise.

What is the SIGN of the relationship between rs_percentile and forward 5/10/20-day return? The decision hinges on this and nothing else. At decision time corr(rs_score, fwd20d) was -0.68 on a single cohort.

Does rs_percentile discriminate where rs_score could not? Compare forward returns of the top vs bottom percentile tercile RESTRICTED to rows where rs_score == 100. If there is no spread inside the saturated group, the percentile adds nothing and this entry should be resolved as 'no effect' rather than left open.
Is any result carried by one date or one ticker? Drop the largest-contributing trigger date and re-run. If the sign flips, it has not been measured.

If the relationship is NEGATIVE and holds up: the implied change is an RS CEILING (reject over-extended leaders), not the percentile promotion originally proposed. Does the extension data agree, given the 2026-09-09 buy-price drift guard already removed most of the pre-era gap-chasing?

If the relationship is POSITIVE and holds up: what would swapping rs_score for rs_percentile inside compute_final_score have changed about which ticker won each slot, and would that have helped? Re-rank historical cohorts before changing any live code.

decisions.title: Exit-parameter review: the whole Prove-It stack, re-measured as trades accumulate
decisions.decision: The shipped exit stack (Prove-It Phase 1 1.0%/day-0 then 3.0%; Phase 2 arms at a +2% peak and floors at -1% of entry; profit ladder +5% -> 1.5% trail) stands unchanged. Re-confirmed 2026-09-18 on 52 closed trades: SHIPPED is +$10,669 against the exits that actually happened (+$10,762 for the full live bot including scale-out), the best challenger is +$202 (inside noise), and ZERO winners are harmed. This entry exists to force that measurement to be repeated on a schedule rather than assumed.
decisions.rationale: Every exit threshold was originally tuned on SEVENTEEN closed trades, and every ADR behind them says that is too few to trust. This entry is the ACTIVE half of the review schedule in AGENTS.md, which is otherwise passive: a date in a markdown table only fires if a human happens to read the file, so a review can be missed silently and a provisional number can ossify into a 'fact'. min_closed_trades is deliberately NULL: this review is DATE-driven, and gating it on a trade count would let a slow month stall it indefinitely - which is precisely the failure mode being removed. The review itself reports n first and may legitimately conclude 'sample barely moved, skip'. The dates are a prompt, not an obligation to change something.
review_questions: How many closed trades now? Report n FIRST, every time. Below ~30 the differences are noise. If n has barely moved since the last review, say so and SKIP rather than re-reading noise.

Does the shipped configuration still win? It is the 'ProveIt SHIPPED' row; 'LIVE BASELINE' is the same stop PLUS scale-out and is the correct baseline for any exit-LOOSENING test. Baseline 2026-09-18: +$10,669 (SHIPPED) / +$10,762 (LIVE) on 52 trades. A challenger must beat it by more than ~$500 AND spread that gain over 3+ trades to be a real candidate. Note arming Phase 2 at +3.0% scored +$202 and harmed 6 rather than 8 - below the bar, but watch the sign.

Is any result carried by a single trade? Per-trade deltas are printed for exactly this reason. At the 52-trade baseline the shipped result survived removal of its largest contributor (+$10,669 -> +$8,874, CDNA being 17% of net), with 7 trades each worth over $1,000. Re-check that it still does.

Has anything started harming WINNERS? This is the column that matters most and the one that sank the days-0-1 kill-switch. At the 48-trade baseline all 8 harmed trades were already losers and winners_harmed was ZERO. If a winner starts being clipped, that outweighs loss-cutting gains.

Run --proveit --top 80. It was REPAIRED on 2026-09-18 and now contains the live configuration: the grid includes the live Phase 1 later-band (3.0%) and the live Phase 2 floor (-1.0%), and both shipped_proveit() and live_baseline() are scored rows. --top 80 is required because the grid is 38 rows and the baselines rank below the default 25-row cut. Use live_baseline() (Prove-It PLUS scale-out) as the baseline for any LOOSENING test. Before 2026-09-18 the row labelled SHIPPED modelled the RETIRED pre-2026-09-04 ruleset, so any 'beats shipped by $N' claim from an older --proveit run is void.

Still open: is PROVE_IT_P1_LATER_PCT = 3% correct or CPAY-shaped, and does the Phase 2 floor need a full 1% of slack? Both need a dedicated single-variable sweep - the --proveit rows vary two things at once. Also carry forward the 2026-09-18 observation that PROVE_IT_P2_ARM_GAIN_PCT is NOT at a flat optimum: +1.0% and +1.5% both score worse than the shipped +2.0%, while +3.0% scored +$202 better and harmed 6 trades rather than 8. Below the ~$500 bar, so not shipped - but check whether the sign persists.

Is POWER_HOLD_GAIN_PCT = 10% reachable yet? It was lowered from 20% only because 20% was never reached. If no trade has hit +10% within 21 days, the rule is still dormant and the number is still a guess.

history.note: 2026-09-20 checkpoint, run 3 days early. SHIPPED first at +$10,673; runner-up (arm +1.5%) -$29 and harms one more trade. Cliff fix rejected again at -$1,393 with >300 rising 11->12, on the corrected sample that now CONTAINS NTRA RT1 - the owed re-run is discharged and that caveat is closed. Zero winners harmed; all 8 harmed trades were already losers. Result robust to dropping its largest contributor. No change made. Also replaced the stale 30-trade baseline table in AGENTS.md and corrected it to cite --cliff rather than --proveit.

Scheduled 2026-09-20 review run two days early (the 20th is a Sunday, so no new data would arrive). n=52 (26 losers, 26 winners). Prove-It SHIPPED (stop only) +$10,669; LIVE BASELINE incl. scale-out +$10,762; retired pre-Prove-It ruleset +$1,643. 24 trades helped, 8 harmed, and ALL 8 harmed were already losers - zero winners harmed. Not carried by one trade: largest contributor CDNA +$1,795 is 17% of net, and net ex-largest is still +$8,874, with seven trades over $1,000 each. Best challenger was arming Phase 2 at a +3.0% peak (+$202, harmed 6 not 8) - inside the ~$500 noise bar, so NOT shipped; flagged to re-check next review. NO PARAMETER CHANGED. The review's main product was a repair to the harness: --proveit's baseline row was labelled SHIPPED but modelled the RETIRED pre-2026-09-04 ruleset, the grid omitted the live Phase 1 later-tier (3.0%) and the live Phase 2 floor (-1.0%), and the default --top 25 hid the baselines. Renamed to retired_pre_proveit_config(), added the live shape/floor to the grid, and added live_baseline() + shipped_proveit() as scored rows.

decisions.title: Breakout failure penalty disabled; tolerances need refitting before any re-enable
decisions.decision: FAILURE_PENALTY_MAX_POINTS ships at 0, disabling the breakout failure penalty. adjusted_score equals final_score, so the buy-loop score floors test the AI-evaluated score directly. _compute_failure_penalty is retained but inert.
decisions.rationale: Replayed over all 16 breakout_learnings rows using each trade's own entry parameters, the penalty returned the maximum for EVERY trade: mean 20.0 on 10 winners and 20.0 on 6 losers. It has zero discriminative power, so disabling it cannot lose information. The cause is that each match tolerance is wider than the observed winner/loser separation on that parameter, making a match guaranteed rather than informative. Disabling needed no extra trades (a statistic with zero variance across all inputs stays uninformative at any n); REFITTING the tolerances does, which is why this entry exists.
decisions.review_command: python3 research/rs_percentile_review.py --insecure   # plus: confirm trigger_history forward-outcome coverage is no longer 16/233 and includes BREAKOUT rows
review_questions: Does trigger_history now carry forward outcomes for a meaningful number of BREAKOUT triggers? If still near zero, the tolerances STILL cannot be fitted - defer again and do not re-enable.
Using those outcomes, is there any tolerance set on which the four parameters actually separate winners from losers on held-out data? If not, retire the penalty permanently rather than retuning it.

Since disabling, have BREAKOUT entries that would previously have been blocked performed worse than those that would have passed? That is the direct test of whether the filter was doing anything useful.

Has the day-0/1 stop-out pattern that generated all six 'failures' changed? If the exit rules stopped producing noise-level losses, the learnings table content is different and any earlier conclusion must be re-derived.

decisions.title: Split execution_agent.py orchestrators (monitor/reconcile/buys) into testable units
decisions.decision: The pure layer of execution_agent.py was extracted on 2026-09-18 (exit_rules.py, indicators.py, market_calendar.py; 5828 -> 4952 lines). The three remaining orchestrators are NOT split yet and the work is deferred, not abandoned.
decisions.rationale: Unlike the pure extraction, this split cannot be byte-identical: monitor_portfolio_intraday (683L, 8 notifier calls, 18 local calls, 9 helpers patched by tests), reconcile_with_ibkr (589L, 14 notifier calls) and run_market_open_buys (537L, 13 notifier calls) are coupled to I/O, so seams must be designed rather than cut. That makes 'the tests still pass' materially weaker evidence than it was for the pure move. Doing it while positions are open risks the code path that enforces the stops on live money. Deferred until the book is quiet.
decisions.baseline: At deferral: monitor_portfolio_intraday 683L / 8 notifier / 18 local / 9 patched helpers; reconcile_with_ibkr 589L / 14 notifier; run_market_open_buys 537L / 13 notifier. execution_agent.py 4952L total, 751 tests passing.
review_questions: Is the book actually quiet, or is the precondition passing on a technicality (e.g. 2 positions both at day 7 and still inside a trailing stop)?
Has patch 054 been live in production long enough to trust? Confirm the agent container is running the split modules and that no import-time failure occurred.
Does the local-LLM workflow still need it? The pure extraction alone may have solved the context problem, in which case this yields maintainability only.
What is the seam? Inject the notifier, or have orchestrators return events for a thin caller to dispatch? Decide before cutting, not during.
Can the split be proven safe without byte-identity? If not, say what evidence replaces it -- 'tests pass' is not sufficient here.

decisions.title: Phase 1 rests on a static STP, not a ratcheting TRAIL order
decisions.decision: Phase 1 of the Prove-It Stop is carried by the static hard-stop leg (hard_stop_price(), which gained a days_held argument and returns entry*(1-p1_pct)*(1-slack) for UNPROVEN positions only) instead of by a trailing percentage. prove_it_trail_pct() returns None for phase1, so no IBKR TRAIL order carries a Phase 1 level and nothing can ratchet. safe_hard_stop() refuses to place any static stop at or above the market. Phase 2 is unchanged. Deliberately NOT extended to proven-but-unarmed positions, which keep the disaster floor (that is the separately-rejected p2_unarmed_keeps_p1 hypothesis).
decisions.rationale: FIXED A DEFECT, not a tuning choice: exit_rules.py documents Phase 1 as a FIXED floor anchored to entry, but place_protective_stops() submits it as orderType='TRAIL', whose anchor ratchets up with the high-water mark. SMTC (2026-09-18) reconciles to the cent: an order intended to rest at $176.91 (entry -2.0%) climbed to $182.11 (entry +0.89%) and sold a winner at +0.76%, 23 minutes after entry. Ten of 49 closed trades carry the signature, netting -$114 across ten slots. A 50-trade replay isolating the ratchet (new --p1ratchet flag) scored +$2,590 for pinning it: +$2,902 recovered on winners, -$313 paid on losers. TWO CAVEATS THAT MUST DRIVE THE REVIEW: (a) +$2,409 of the $2,590 is CPAY ALONE -- ex-CPAY the net is +$181, which is noise, so the dollar figure is NOT a defensible expected value and the decision rests on correctness instead; (b) the prior hypothesis that pinning would leave losers untouched was WRONG -- INCY (-$222) and PTGX (-$91) are losers the ratchet exited sooner, so the trade-off is real, just ~9:1 lopsided.
review_questions: SINGLE-TRADE-CARRY CHECK, ask this first: is the B-A gap still dominated by CPAY? Report the net WITH and WITHOUT the largest single contributor. Baseline was +$2,590 total but only +$181 ex-CPAY.

Has the direction held? Baseline was unanimous: 3/3 winners helped, 2/2 losers hurt. If losers are now hurt by more than winners are helped, the ratchet was cutting losses and this decision must be revisited.
How many trades are affected at all? Baseline was 5 of 50. If it is still ~10%, the rule matters less than the correctness argument implies and that should be said plainly.
Has any NEW trade been sold by a Phase 1 stop resting above entry? That must now be impossible -- if one appears, the fix is not working and this is a live bug, not a review item.
Does the slack dose-response still hold (winners scored +$948 / +$2,320 / +$5,222 at 0.5% / 1.0% / 2.0%)? If it has gone flat, the mechanism model in the harness is wrong.

Would simply widening PROVE_IT_BACKSTOP_SLACK_PCT to 2% have scored as well? It did on the baseline (+$10,692 vs +$10,644) -- if it still does, note that it is a one-env-var alternative, but do NOT adopt it: a stop that CAN rise above entry stays wrong regardless of its expected value.

decisions.title: Phase 2 ladder width and the power-hold trigger must be retuned together, and not before slot cost is modelled
decisions.decision: NO live parameter changed. TRAIL_PROFIT_TIERS stays at +5% -> 1.5% and POWER_HOLD_GAIN_PCT stays at 10.0. What shipped is measurement capability: research/exit_rule_replay.py gained a run-on window (--runon / --runon-days, default 30) that extends price history past each realised exit, and gained a model of the power hold (power_hold_gain / power_hold_trail / trigger / duration on ExitConfig, applied in simulate_proveit). Both are strictly opt-in: with --runon off, runon_from stays 0 and every other sweep replays byte-identically (verified against the pre-change --ladder table to the dollar).
decisions.rationale: Two findings. (1) METHODOLOGICAL: every sweep before this one truncated bars at the realised exit, so a rule that would have held LONGER ran out of history exactly when the live rule sold and scored a delta of zero -- handed the live exit price for free. Tightening is unaffected (it fires before truncation); loosening was unmeasurable BY CONSTRUCTION, which is why the truncated --ladder sweep decays perfectly monotonically as the trail widens. (2) SUBSTANTIVE: power hold at +10% is not unreachable for want of +10% names -- 13 of 50 closed trades reached +10% within 21 days of entry, but the bot was still holding exactly ONE of them, because the +5% ladder rung clamps the trail to 1.5% and sells at roughly half the trigger. Power hold at +10% replays byte-identically to shipped at 30%/15%/10% trail widths: it never fires. The two rules are mutually inconsistent and cannot be retuned independently. WHY NOTHING SHIPPED: with the run-on window, ladder 5% (+$5,685) and 8% (+$5,935) beat shipped, but ~65% of each is ECO alone, harmed rises 12 -> 18, and -- decisively -- slot opportunity cost is entirely unmodelled. MAX_POSITIONS is 5, so holding a winner 30 extra days blocks the next breakout, and no price-path replay can price that. All 52 trades also fall in one market regime, which is the weakest possible setting for a hold-longer result.

baseline.power_hold_10pct_note: identical to shipped at every trail width -- never fires

review_questions: BLOCKING PRECONDITION, check this before reading any dollar figure: can the harness price slot opportunity cost yet? MAX_POSITIONS is 5, and every run-on figure assumes a position can be held 30 extra days for free. Until a replay can model the breakouts NOT taken because a slot was occupied, a positive run-on net is an upper bound and not a reason to widen the ladder. If the answer is still no, the correct verdict is 'still blocked' -- do not ship a ladder change on price-path evidence alone.

SINGLE-TRADE-CARRY CHECK: is the ladder-5%/8% advantage still ~65% one trade? Baseline was ECO +$3,794 of a +$5,685 net; ex-ECO it is +$1,891 over 23 trades. Report the net with and without the largest single contributor.

REGIME CHECK: do the trades now span more than one market regime? A hold-longer result measured entirely in a rising tape is close to uninformative. If the sample is still one regime, say so and discount accordingly.

REACHABILITY: re-run the reachability table. Has the count of trades reaching +10% within 21 days WHILE STILL HELD moved off 1? If it has not, power hold remains inert and lowering POWER_HOLD_GAIN_PCT in isolation is still the wrong lever -- the ladder sells first.

DOWNSIDE: track harmed and >300 alongside the net. Baseline was 12 -> 18 harmed going from shipped to ladder 5%. A widened give-back that improves the net by clipping fewer winners while materially worsening losers is not obviously the trade you want on a 5-slot book.

history.note: Re-measured against the CORRECT live baseline (ladder 1.5% + scale-out 33%@+4%, both already shipped). An earlier read of +$6,429 was taken against a no-scale-out baseline and is withdrawn. True figures: remainder trail 3% = -$1,350; 5% = +$4,308 but ECO is 59% of net and ex-top-3 is -$1,014; 8% = +$4,495, ECO 56%, ex-top-3 -$1,801. Every positive result is outlier-carried, so the deferral stands. Worst single-trade loss is unchanged at -$1,269 across ALL variants, confirming the loss side is not what binds. Slot opportunity cost remains unmodelled and is still a blocking precondition. See decisions/2026-09-18_scaleout-runon-bias-and-concentration.md.

Drawdown-conditional rung tested (--clean --runon-days 30) against the FULL live bot incl. scale-out. LIVE BASELINE wins outright at +$10,762; every loosening scores lower (3% flat +$8,426; 5% flat +$6,611) and harms more trades (8 -> 11-13). The condition is a flat widening in disguise: 14/15 (93%) of trades reaching +5% qualify at dd<=3%, because Phase 1 already exits at -1%/-3% so survivors are shallow-drawdown by construction. Loosening also REDUCES the winner delta (+4,209 -> +1,872): a wider rung rides faders down rather than holding runners. Loss side identical in every row (worst -$1,269, >300 = 10). Exit is not the bottleneck.

decisions.title: Is the missing right tail an EXIT problem or an ENTRY problem? Measure on the trigger population, not on taken trades
decisions.decision: NOTHING shipped. This is an OPEN QUESTION with a defined measurement, recorded so it cannot be forgotten. The bot's realised return distribution has no right tail: across 52 closed trades the best result is LPG +6.47% and NOTHING exceeds +7%, while nothing is worse than -6.25%. The loss side is now demonstrably well controlled (since the Prove-It Stop shipped 2026-09-04 the worst loss is -1.62%, payoff ratio 1.96, expectancy +$183/trade), so the deficit is entirely on the winner side. Repeated attempts to fix that by LOOSENING THE EXIT have all failed the concentration test -- see ladder-width-runon. The hypothesis this entry exists to test is therefore that the binding constraint is UPSTREAM of the exit: either the screener is not producing stocks that run, or the bot is systematically choosing the wrong triggers from those it does produce.
decisions.rationale: There is a concrete and troubling preliminary signal that must be confirmed or killed. On the TAKEN trades, 13/50 reached +10% within 21 days and only 1/50 reached +20%. On the matured rows of trigger_history -- i.e. the breakouts the screener FIRED, whether or not the bot bought them -- 20/50 reached +10% and 8/50 reached +20%. If that gap survives an overlap check, the screener is generating right-tail candidates and the bot's SELECTION among them is destroying the tail before any exit rule is reached. That would make trigger ranking, not trail width, the single highest-leverage thing in the system. It must not be asserted on 50 half-matured rows, which is exactly why this waits.
measurement_plan: A. SELECTION: for each trading day, split matured trigger_history rows into TAKEN (a trade_history/portfolio row exists for that ticker within ~2 sessions of triggered_at) and PASSED OVER. Compare max_gain_20d_pct distributions. Confirm or kill the 8/50-vs-1/50 signal FIRST -- if the bot's picks underperform its own passed-over triggers, nothing else in this plan matters.

B. PREDICTION: per-feature discrimination of max_gain_20d_pct >= 10% (secondary: >= 20%), over quality_score, technical_score, final_score, adjusted_score, rs_score, rs_percentile (once populated), atr_pct, volume_surge, pivot_distance_pct, liquidity_score, sentiment_score, failure_penalty, trigger_type. Report AUC and decile lift per feature.

C. HONESTY GUARDS, mandatory: (i) time-split -- fit on the older half by triggered_at, report on the newer half, never in-sample; (ii) permutation baseline -- shuffle the labels and report the AUC the same search finds on noise, because with ~13 features the best in-sample AUC will look impressive on pure noise; (iii) report n for every cell.

D. SLOT COST: for each day the book was full (open_positions == MAX_POSITIONS), count triggers that fired and could not be bought, and total their realised max_gain_20d_pct. This is the opportunity cost of holding winners longer, and it is the BLOCKING PRECONDITION on ladder-width-runon -- that entry cannot be resolved until this number exists.

E. SIZING: only if B finds a feature that survives C. Replay conviction-weighted sizing (weight by the surviving feature) against the shipped equal-weight rule position_size = available_cash / remaining_slots. If B finds nothing, equal-weight is CORRECT and this step is skipped, not fudged.
decisions.decision_rule: TWO sample gates, both required. (1) >= 150 matured trigger rows. (2) >= 20 DISTINCT trigger dates -- row count is not sample size. On 2026-09-18 all 50 matured rows came from just FOUR scan dates (2026-08-14..19), so they are four observations of market regime wearing fifty hats: every row on one day shares the same tape, breadth and sector rotation, and a feature can look predictive purely because its day ran. research/entry_quality_review.py prints a loud warning below 20 dates. Beyond the gates: a feature is actionable ONLY if it holds AUC >= 0.60 on the HELD-OUT half, shows monotone decile lift, and clears the permutation baseline by a visible margin. If nothing clears the bar, the honest conclusion is that entry quality is not measurable from the features currently stored, and the next move is to store better ones -- NOT to ship a weak ranker.

baseline_at_decision.note: trigger-population figures are from 50 matured rows of 245 and the TAKEN/PASSED overlap has NOT yet been checked. They are a reason to measure, NOT a finding.
baseline_at_decision.correction: The 8/50-vs-1/50 framing that motivated this entry was WRONG and is withdrawn. It compared the taken trades' REALISED returns against the trigger population's MAX_GAIN -- two different measures. Measured like for like, the bot's TAKEN triggers have a median 20-day max gain of +12.83% versus +3.76% for those it passed over (AUC 0.623). Selection is ADDING value, not destroying it. The bot buys stocks that do run and then exits before they do. On 4 dates this is indicative only.
baseline_at_decision.rs_backfilled: 2026-09-18: all 245 trigger_history rows backfilled by research/backfill_rs_percentile.py (no lookahead; validated to exact equality against all 13 live-written daily_triggers rows). The 0/245 was a pipeline-timing artifact, not a defect -- the migration was applied and daily_triggers was always correct.
baseline_at_decision.rs_score_saturation: 185/245 rows (76%) sit at the clipped maximum of 100
baseline_at_decision.first_run_5d_horizon: 200 rows / 19 dates; all four RS variants rank top-4 (best rs_excess_return AUC 0.608) but the permutation baseline is 0.593 -- NO SIGNAL. Horizons disagree (rs_percentile 0.370 on the 20d sample).

review_questions: Are there >= 20 distinct trigger dates yet? If not, stop: the rows are clustered within days and the effective sample is far smaller than n.
Does rs_excess_return (unclipped) beat rs_score (clipped at +10%) on the 20-day horizon? 76% of rows saturate rs_score, so this is the specific thing the percentile was built to test.
Do the bot's TAKEN triggers underperform the triggers it passed over, on the same days? (If yes, ranking is the whole problem and everything else is secondary.)
Does ANY entry-time feature separate the >= +10% population on the HELD-OUT half, or only in-sample?
What AUC does the same search find on permuted labels? If the real best barely beats it, report 'no signal' and stop.
What did a blocked slot actually cost, in dollars of forgone max_gain_20d_pct?
Is rs_percentile populated yet? It was 0/245 on 2026-09-18 and is the single feature most likely to carry CAN SLIM's 'L'.

revisit.why: 245 trigger rows exist but only 50 had matured 20-day outcomes on 2026-09-18. 150 is the point at which a held-out half is ~75 rows -- thin, but enough to distinguish a real AUC of 0.65 from noise. Gating on matured triggers rather than closed trades is deliberate: this question is answered on the trigger population, which grows several times faster than the traded one.
